brief: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching.

requirements.evidence: drawer:0#0,0#cut fills the south half of the north half base at (0,0).

requirements.requirement: One spike on that same cell
requirements.evidence: spike:0#0,-1|0,0|1,-1 stands at a north corner of cell (0,0).

requirements.requirement: Drawer and spike at the very same corner of the cell
requirements.evidence: The configurator refuses it. A spike at a corner of the drawer's half blocks the drawer (SPIKE_CLASH), and with the drawer in place none of the cell's corners are offered for a spike. The spike stands at a different corner instead.
The only accepted spike corner is on the base's north side, away from the drawer, so the two parts don't touch.

finish.summary:
I couldn't put a drawer and a spike on the same corner of the same cell. The configurator doesn't allow it. I tested it both ways on cell (0,0), a north half base with its drawer filling the south half. With the drawer in place, none of the cell's corners were offered for a spike. With a spike at the corner where cells (0,0), (0,1) and (1,0) meet, adding the drawer was refused with SPIKE_CLASH ("a spike stands at a corner of this cell the drawer (south half) would fill"). Neither of the two corners on the cut line was offered either.

What I built instead: the north half base at (0,0) with its drawer (drawer:0#0,0#cut). I put full bases at (0,-1) and (1,-1). The spike stands at the north corner where cells (0,0), (0,-1) and (1,-1) meet (spike:0#0,-1|0,0|1,-1). The spike and drawer are on the same cell but at different corners, and they don't touch. I closed the open faces with end caps and bolted the joints, as the standard steps require; that brings it to 17 parts. The build check found no errors and no collisions.

M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
